A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SRL work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original continuous-control experiments, FAS comparisons, stochastic-timestep evaluations and a latent-space Walker2d experiment in its appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds experiments involving GPM, multiple SAC training timesteps, randomized frame-skipping and broader TempoRL evaluation.

M1.justification: Equation 5 corrects the documented actor-loss summation endpoint from J to J−1, matching the stated J-action sequence. The GRU actor, dynamics model, critics, Algorithm 1 and latent-space extension otherwise remain unchanged. This correction does not establish that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: V3 adds Pendulum-v1, expanding the benchmark suite from ten to eleven continuous-control environments. This is distinct from the InvertedPendulum and InvertedDoublePendulum environments already evaluated in v1. The stochastic-timestep scenario and latent Walker2d evaluation were already present.

E2.justification: V3 adds GPM as a direct comparator in four environments (Figure 4) and randomized SAC, SAC-R, in Appendix A.10. TempoRL, already compared with latent SRL on Walker2d in v1, receives a broader seven-environment evaluation in Table 7. The latter reports rewards and sequence lengths rather than a matched FAS comparison.

E3.justification: V3 trains SAC at J = 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16, enabling comparisons beyond v1's baseline trained at the default timestep. It also introduces randomized frame-skipping during SAC training, specifies GPM plan-length choices and adds TempoRL maximum-length tuning. The original SRL update schedule, common hyperparameters and stochastic-timestep evaluation procedure remain.

E4.justification: The SAC timestep sweep and randomized frame-skipping analysis test whether adapting baseline training closes the frequency-robustness gap. These add substantial controls absent from v1. Existing stochastic-timestep correlations and latent-space analyses are retained; the additional matched-J learning-curve figures primarily redisplay the expanded comparisons.

E5.justification: The main FAS tables retain five-trial means and standard deviations, and frequency plots retain standard-error reporting. V3 Table 7 newly specifies averaging TempoRL results over ten seeds. This adds experiment-specific seed information without establishing an increase in runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Numerous retained FAS entries change: Hopper SRL-16 changes from 0.44 ± 0.04 in v1 Table 2 to 0.57 ± 0.02 in v3 Table 3, while Lunar Lander SRL-16 changes from 0.89 ± 0.05 to 0.84 ± 0.03. New comparator results substantially expand the evidence and reveal stronger SAC performance on Swimmer. These are reported revisions, not verified improvements under identical experimental conditions.

T1.justification: Equation 5 removes an extra terminal loss term by changing the summation endpoint from J to J−1; the accompanying sequence range is corrected accordingly. This resolves a mathematical inconsistency with the stated sequence length. Other substantive equations, including the latent temporal-consistency objective, are retained; neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the online-planning claim from superior FAS to comparable FAS. The introduction adds an explicit claim of outperforming GPM. The central contributions—sequence generation at low decision frequencies, model-based training with model-free control, and FAS—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations for SAC's Swimmer advantage and GPM's weak sequence generalization, plus discussion of delay handling and hardware constraints in Section 2 and Appendix A.3. Future work qualifies infinite-horizon control as near-infinite control in noiseless settings with corrections. Existing modeling-error limitations and latent-space interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds an official SRL repository link, and the new comparisons document plan-length choices and selected TempoRL maximum sequence lengths. Existing network sizes, optimization parameters, hardware specifications and environment-budget tables are retained. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the repository's availability or contents.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning around temporally correlated exploration, including GPM, TLA and related exploration methods. It connects the evaluation to Dulac-Arnold's real-world RL challenges and discusses hardware acceleration and software optimization alternatives. The MPC distinction also shifts from requiring an already accurate model to requiring model access during deployment.

P1.justification: V3 revises the motivation, delay discussion, experimental narrative and future-work prose, merges the macro-action and action-repetition subsections, and adds appendix headings. The main section order and much of the method, neuroscience and existing appendix exposition remain intact; these are targeted revisions rather than a wholesale narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, the combined FAS table becomes separate SAC and SRL tables, and learning and frequency plots are separated and expanded. V3 adds GPM and randomized-SAC displays and matched-J curve panels, while relocating existing illustrations and appendix material. Presentation changes are substantial, although several appendix pages become sparse and some comparison panels are very small.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially addresses an important weakness in v1: the main SAC baseline was trained at the default timestep. SAC-J and SAC-R controls test whether training adaptation explains SRL's advantage, while GPM supplies a close sequence-generating comparator. The Swimmer exception and moderated online-planning claim make the conclusions more informative. Unexplained FAS revisions and inconsistently updated illustrations, such as the Hopper curves in v3 Figures 2 and 9, remain drawbacks, but the stronger comparative evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
